sentences.en: So we did a podcast on Sherlock Holmes.
sentences.zh: 我们之前做过一期关于福尔摩斯的播客。

sentences.en: So we've done one on a fictional character already, and this is our second one on a purely fictional character.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经做过一个虚构人物了，这是我们第二个纯虚构人物的专题。

sentences.en: And I think they make a nice pair, actually, because in their different ways, Holmes and Bond are both representatives of Britain and Britishness.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得它们搭配得很好，因为福尔摩斯和邦德以各自不同的方式，都是英国和英国性的代表。

sentences.en: But they're also fascinating historical phenomena.
sentences.zh: 但它们也是迷人的历史现象。

sentences.en: So Holmes is obviously sort of late Victorian, Edwardian Britain, and Bond is a creation of, well, the post-World War II, 1950s, 1960s world.
sentences.zh: 福尔摩斯显然是维多利亚时代晚期到爱德华时代的英国，而邦德则是二战后，即20世纪50年代和60年代世界的产物。

sentences.en: But compared to Holmes, I mean, there's so much in Bond that just kind of, well, reeks of his age, I guess.
sentences.zh: 但与福尔摩斯相比，邦德身上有太多东西，怎么说呢，散发着那个时代的臭味，我想。

sentences.en: I mean, the attitudes to race, to sexuality, to all kinds of things are, by our standards, it's only a few decades on.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对种族、性以及各种事物的态度，以我们的标准来看，虽然才过了几十年，

sentences.en: But, I mean, it seems like a completely different age, whereas Holmes, oddly, seems a much more contemporary character.
sentences.zh: 但看起来就像是一个完全不同的时代，而福尔摩斯奇怪地看起来更像是一个当代角色。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我觉得确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think that's partly because Ian Fleming was reactionary, even by the standards of the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为部分原因是伊恩·弗莱明即使以50年代的标准来看，也是个反动派。

sentences.en: I mean, he was intensely reactionary.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他极其反动。

sentences.en: And even at the time, some people sort of remarked on that, and there's a very famous review.
sentences.zh: 即使在当时，也有人注意到了这一点，有一篇非常著名的书评。

sentences.en: So for people who don't like James Bond, they'll enjoy this.
sentences.zh: 所以对于不喜欢詹姆斯·邦德的人来说，他们会喜欢这个。

sentences.en: This was Paul Johnson in The New Statesman in 1958.
sentences.zh: 这是保罗·约翰逊1958年在《新政治家》上发表的评论。

sentences.en: So he's just been reading Dr. No.
sentences.zh: 他刚读完《诺博士》。

sentences.en: And he says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: I've just finished what is, without any doubt, the nastiest book I've ever read.
sentences.zh: 我刚读完这本毫无疑问是我读过最恶心的书。

sentences.en: I had to suppress a strong impulse to throw the thing away.
sentences.zh: 我不得不压抑住一种强烈的冲动，想把这东西扔掉。

sentences.en: There are three basic ingredients in Dr. No, all unhealthy, all thoroughly English.
sentences.zh: 《诺博士》有三个基本要素，都不健康，而且都非常“英国”。

sentences.en: The sadism of a schoolboy bully, the mechanical two-dimensional sex longings of a frustrated adolescent, and the crude snob cravings of a suburban adult.
sentences.zh: 小学生霸凌者的虐待狂倾向，受挫青少年机械的二维性渴望，以及郊区成年人粗俗的势利追求。

sentences.en: Mr. Fleming has no literary skill, and this seems to me far more dangerous than straight pornography.
sentences.zh: 弗莱明先生没有任何文学技巧，这在我看来比纯粹的色情作品危险得多。

sentences.en: The novel is badly written to the point of incoherence.
sentences.zh: 这部小说写得太烂了，简直语无伦次。

sentences.en: And that sort of stuff about snobbery, sexism, and sadism, I mean, they're what we Bond fans love about James Bond.
sentences.zh: 而那种关于势利、性别歧视和虐待狂的东西，我是说，那正是我们邦德迷喜欢詹姆斯·邦德的地方。

sentences.en: Is it, though?
sentences.zh: 真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think they're very important elements of it, actually.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为它们实际上是非常重要的元素。

sentences.en: But there's a huge chasm, isn't there, between the novels and the films?
sentences.zh: 但小说和电影之间有巨大的鸿沟，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because I was the Roger Moore generation.
sentences.zh: 因为我是罗杰·摩尔那一代的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And to me, it seemed pretty much on a level with Carry On.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它看起来和《随身变》系列差不多。

sentences.en: I mean, it seemed about as sadistic as a Carry On film, i.e. not very.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它看起来和《随身变》电影一样有虐待狂倾向，也就是没多少。

sentences.en: It was kind of smutty, and that was about the limit of it.
sentences.zh: 它有点下流，这就是极限了。

sentences.en: That's all you see in it, the smuts.
sentences.zh: 你看到的只有那些下流的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I think because of that, I've never really, I mean, I never felt, I've never really taken James Bond seriously.
sentences.zh: 是啊，所以我认为正因为如此，我从来没有，我是说，我从来没觉得，我从来没真正认真对待过詹姆斯·邦德。

sentences.en: I mean, he seems about as serious as Kenneth WilliaMs.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他看起来和肯尼斯·威廉姆斯一样严肃。

sentences.en: Well, I think the Roger Moore films, which people of our age probably take as the template, are, to some extent, aberrations within the sequence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们这个年纪的人可能把罗杰·摩尔的电影当作模板，但在整个系列中，它们在某种程度上是异类。

sentences.en: So there are more non-Roger Moores than there are Roger Moores before and after.
sentences.zh: 所以罗杰·摩尔之前的和之后的非罗杰·摩尔电影更多。

sentences.en: And the Roger Moores are not representative in any way of Fleming's vision.
sentences.zh: 而且罗杰·摩尔的电影在任何方面都不能代表弗莱明的构想。

sentences.en: Now, obviously, they work as kind of parodies, to some extent.
sentences.zh: 当然，它们在某种程度上确实起到了模仿的作用。

sentences.en: They're parodies of themselves.
sentences.zh: 它们是对自身的模仿。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So they're kind of Austin Powers before Austin Powers.
sentences.zh: 所以它们就像是《王牌大贱谍》之前的《王牌大贱谍》。

sentences.en: They are Austin Powers.
sentences.zh: 它们就是《王牌大贱谍》。

sentences.en: But that's one of the things why I don't think Austin Powers is quite as funny as lots of other people think, because it's parodying something that was already parodying itself.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么我觉得《王牌大贱谍》不像其他人认为的那么好笑的原因之一，因为它模仿的东西本身就在模仿自己。

sentences.en: But I think, well, I mean, maybe if you're a sceptic, I need to persuade you that James Bond matters.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，嗯，我是说，也许如果你是个怀疑论者，我需要说服你詹姆斯·邦德很重要。

sentences.en: No, well, I'm not a sceptic.
sentences.zh: 不，我不是怀疑论者。

sentences.en: I'm not a sceptic.
sentences.zh: 我不是怀疑论者。

sentences.en: But because I grew up with the Roger Moore one, and then because basically the only other ones I've seen are the Maurice, the Daniel Craig ones.
sentences.zh: 但因为我是看着罗杰·摩尔的电影长大的，而且基本上我唯一看过的其他电影就是莫里斯，也就是丹尼尔·克雷格的那几部。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Where he's kind of earnest and tortured.
sentences.zh: 在那里他显得很严肃和痛苦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And basically, I guess, trying to square the original material with the very different cultural mores of the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我想，是在试图将原始素材与21世纪截然不同的文化习俗相调和。

sentences.en: I hadn't properly realised kind of what the novels were like.
sentences.zh: 我之前并没有真正意识到小说是什么样的。

sentences.en: And so.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: They're quite strong stuff, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 它们内容相当劲爆，不是吗？

sentences.en: They are quite strong stuff.
sentences.zh: 确实相当劲爆。

sentences.en: I mean, the funny thing is, I don't think they're very.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有趣的是，我不觉得它们很……

sentences.en: And it's brought out even more clearly in the Simon Winder book than in your book.
sentences.zh: 而且在西蒙·温德的书里比在你的书里表现得更清楚。

sentences.en: So could we just look at Ian Fleming?
sentences.zh: 那我们能看看伊恩·弗莱明吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So tell me about Ian Fleming and where this stuff is coming from.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说伊恩·弗莱明，以及这些东西的来源。

sentences.en: So Ian Fleming, he's a very strange man.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·弗莱明，他是个非常奇怪的人。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这么说很公平。

sentences.en: He's born in 1908.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1908年。

sentences.en: His father's a Tory MP, Valentine Fleming.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是保守党议员瓦伦丁·弗莱明。

sentences.en: They're from a family that made a lot of money in Jute, and they've moved south from Dundee originally in the Victorian period and become very rich.
sentences.zh: 他们来自一个靠黄麻生意发了大财的家族，最初在维多利亚时期从邓迪搬到南方，变得非常富有。

sentences.en: So his father is a Tory MP and a barrister and a merchant banker.
sentences.zh: 所以他的父亲是保守党议员、大律师和商业银行家。

sentences.en: And his father, Valentine, is killed in the First World War in Picardy in 1917.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲瓦伦丁在1917年第一次世界大战期间死于皮卡第。

sentences.en: Churchill wrote an obituary of him that appeared in, I think, The Times.
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔为他写了一篇讣告，我想是登在《泰晤士报》上的。

sentences.en: And Fleming, Ian, you know, what is he, nine or so when his father dies?
sentences.zh: 弗莱明，伊恩，你知道，他父亲去世时他才九岁左右？

sentences.en: And that obviously has a colossal impact on him.
sentences.zh: 那显然对他产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And he has a picture of his father, and he's always trying to live up to his father's tremendous heroism.
sentences.zh: 他有一张父亲的照片，他总是试图不辜负父亲那种巨大的英雄主义。

sentences.en: The other thing that Ian Fleming suffers from is he's a younger brother, his older brother, Peter.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·弗莱明遭受的另一件事是他是一个弟弟，他的哥哥是彼得。

sentences.en: So Peter Fleming is a far more impressive man in every way.
sentences.zh: 所以彼得·弗莱明在各方面都是一个令人印象深刻得多的人。

sentences.en: He's kind of forgotten now.
sentences.zh: 他现在快被遗忘了。

sentences.en: There's a great sort of tragedy in that everybody remembers Ian Fleming, but not Peter Fleming.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种悲剧，每个人都记得伊恩·弗莱明，却不记得彼得·弗莱明。

sentences.en: Peter Fleming is a genuine hero and an adventurer.
sentences.zh: 彼得·弗莱明是一位真正的英雄和冒险家。

sentences.en: So he's married to Celia Johnson, the actress who's in Brief Encounter.
sentences.zh: 他娶了西莉亚·约翰逊，就是演《相见恨晚》的那位女演员。

sentences.en: So he's got a film star wife.
sentences.zh: 所以他有一个电影明星妻子。

sentences.en: He's famous because he goes on an expedition to find the explorer Percy Fawcett, who had gone on this expedition of his own to find the lost city of Zed in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 他很有名，因为他去探险寻找探险家珀西·福塞特，福塞特曾独自去寻找巴西的失落之城“Zed”。

sentences.en: Kind of El Dorado queSt.
sentences.zh: 类似于寻找黄金国。

sentences.en: El Dorado.
sentences.zh: 黄金国。

sentences.en: So Peter Fleming, when he's a young man, goes to try and find him.
sentences.zh: 所以彼得·弗莱明年轻时就去试图寻找他。

sentences.en: Doesn't find him, but writes a best-selling book called Brazilian Adventure, which is a kind of true story of this incredible journey.
sentences.zh: 没找到，但写了一本畅销书叫《巴西探险》，讲述了这段不可思议旅程的真实故事。

sentences.en: Then he writes another book about an incredible journey called News from Tartary.
sentences.zh: 然后他又写了另一本关于不可思议旅程的书，叫《鞑靼新闻》。

sentences.en: So he's done an overland journey in the 1930s from Peking to Kashmir, through kind of China, over the Himalayas, all this sort of...
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪30年代进行了一次陆路旅行，从北京到克什米尔，穿过中国，翻越喜马拉雅山，所有这些……

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: He's an amazing man.
sentences.zh: 他是个了不起的人。

sentences.en: That's also what I learned.
sentences.zh: 这也是我学到的。

sentences.en: He was the first person to be richly cursed at a revived witch ceremony.
sentences.zh: 他是第一个在复兴的女巫仪式上被恶毒诅咒的人。

sentences.en: Which, according to Dr. Robin Douglas, who told me this on Twitter, was carried out by a group of Oxford students.
sentences.zh: 据在推特上告诉我的罗宾·道格拉斯博士说，这是由一群牛津学生进行的。

sentences.en: Well, he was at Oxford and he was a member of the Bullingdon Club.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在牛津，是布灵顿俱乐部的成员。

sentences.en: He was a member of the Bullingdon Club, but the curse clearly didn't work because he had this tremendous life.
sentences.zh: 他是布灵顿俱乐部的成员，但诅咒显然没起作用，因为他度过了如此辉煌的一生。

sentences.en: Well, but he didn't become a famous noveliSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但他没成为著名的小说家。

sentences.en: No, he didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没有。

sentences.en: Well, it's only because of Peter Fleming, by the way, that Ian Fleming becomes a novelist at all because his brother pulls strings for him.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，伊恩·弗莱明能成为小说家完全是因为彼得·弗莱明，因为他哥哥为他走了后门。

sentences.en: So Ian Fleming has this father and this brother who are, in their different ways, kind of symbols of British pluck and derring-do and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以伊恩·弗莱明有这样一个父亲和哥哥，他们以各自的方式，是英国勇气和胆识的象征。

sentences.en: They are absolutely the men...
sentences.zh: 他们绝对是那种男人……

sentences.en: And masculinity.

sentences.en: They're the men you would want to be.
sentences.zh: 他们是你想要成为的那种男人。

sentences.zh: 而伊恩·弗莱明本人却是个彻头彻尾的失败者和窝囊废。

sentences.en: So he goes to Eton and he's not academic.
sentences.zh: 他去了伊顿公学，但学习不好。

sentences.en: They put him in the army class at Eton so that he can go to SandhurSt.
sentences.zh: 他们把他放进伊顿的军校班，这样他就能去桑赫斯特皇家军事学院。

sentences.en: But he goes to Sandhurst and he's a failure.
sentences.zh: 但他去了桑赫斯特，结果失败了。

sentences.en: He gets gonorrhea from a prostitute and has to pull out of SandhurSt.
sentences.zh: 他从妓女那里得了淋病，不得不退出桑赫斯特。

sentences.en: He applies for the foreign office and he fails the entrance exaMs.
sentences.zh: 他申请外交部，结果没通过入学考试。

sentences.en: He goes into banking and he fails at that.
